title: Λέων καὶ ὄνος καὶ ἀλώπηξ
titleEn: The Lion, the Donkey and the Fox
part: The Lion, the Donkey and the Fox (Chambry 209)
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 209. Text as printed, including Chambry's editorial punctuation (« »). Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Λέων καὶ ὄνος καὶ ἀλώπηξ κοινωνίαν εἰς ἀλλήλους σπεισάμενοι ἐξῆλθον εἰς ἄγραν.
sentences.tr: Leōn kai onos kai alōpēx koinōnian eis allēlous speisamenoi exēlthon eis agran.
sentences.l: A lion and a donkey and a fox, having poured a libation of partnership toward one another, went out to the chase.
sentences.i: A lion, a donkey and a fox sealed a partnership with one another and went out to the chase.
sentences.n: σπένδομαι is to pour the libation that ratifies an agreement; the wine comes first and the treaty follows from it. The three partners are named in order of strength.

sentences.t: Πολλὴν δὲ αὐτῶν συλλαβόντων, ὁ λέων προσέταξε τῷ ὄνῳ διελεῖν αὐτοῖς.
sentences.tr: Pollēn de autōn syllabontōn, ho leōn prosetaxe tōi onōi dielein autois.
sentences.l: And they having caught much, the lion ordered the donkey to divide it for them.
sentences.n: πολλήν is feminine, agreeing with the ἄγραν of the previous sentence which the Greek does not trouble to repeat: much game.

sentences.t: Τοῦ δὲ τρεῖς μοίρας ἐξ ἴσου ποιήσαντος, καὶ ἐκλέξασθαι αὐτῷ παραινοῦντος, ὁ λέων ἀγανακτήσας ἁλλόμενος κατεθοινήσατο καὶ τῇ ἀλώπεκι μερίσαι προσέταξεν.
sentences.tr: Tou de treis moiras ex isou poiēsantos, kai eklexasthai autōi parainountos, ho leōn aganaktēsas hallomenos katethoinēsato kai tēi alōpeki merisai prosetaxen.
sentences.l: And he having made three shares on an equal footing, and urging him to choose, the lion, having grown angry, sprang and made a banquet of him, and ordered the fox to divide.
sentences.i: When the donkey had made three equal shares and was urging him to take his pick, the lion flew into a rage, sprang on him and ate him up, and ordered the fox to make the division.
sentences.n: ἐξ ἴσου is 'on equal terms' — the donkey's mistake stated in two words. κατεθοινήσατο is built on θοίνη, a feast: not merely eating but banqueting on him. The offence is not the size of the shares but the equality, which makes the lion one partner among three.

sentences.t: Ἡ δὲ πάντα εἰς μίαν μερίδα συναθροίσασα καὶ μικρὰ ἑαυτῇ ὑπολιπομένη παρῄνει αὐτῷ ἑλέσθαι.
sentences.tr: Hē de panta eis mian merida synathroisasa kai mikra heautēi hypolipomenē parēinei autōi helesthai.
sentences.l: And she, having heaped everything into one portion and having left a few small things for herself, urged him to choose.
sentences.n: ὑπολιπομένη is middle, 'having left behind for herself'. The fox uses the same verb of urging as the donkey did, παρῄνει, and only the arithmetic has changed.

sentences.t: Ἐρομένου δὲ αὐτὴν τοῦ λέοντος τίς αὐτὴν οὕτω διανέμειν ἐδίδαξεν, ἡ ἀλώπηξ εἶπεν· « Ἡ τοῦ ὄνου συμφορά. »
sentences.tr: Eromenou de autēn tou leontos tis autēn houtō dianemein edidaxen, hē alōpēx eipen· « Hē tou onou symphora. »
sentences.l: And the lion having asked her who had taught her to divide in this way, the fox said: « The donkey's misfortune. »
sentences.n: A genitive absolute with the whole question folded inside it. συμφορά is what befalls a creature, the thing that happened to it — here a single word doing the work of the entire preceding scene.

sentences.t: Ὁ λόγος δηλοῖ ὅτι σωφρονισμὸς γίνεται τοῖς ἀνθρώποις τὰ τῶν πέλας δυστυχήματα.
sentences.tr: Ho logos dēloi hoti sōphronismos ginetai tois anthrōpois ta tōn pelas dystychēmata.
sentences.l: The story shows that the misfortunes of those close at hand become a bringing to one's senses for men.
sentences.i: The story shows that men are brought to their senses by the misfortunes of those near them.
sentences.n: τὰ δυστυχήματα is the subject and takes a singular verb, γίνεται — the regular rule for neuter plurals. οἱ πέλας, 'those nearby', is the ordinary word for one's neighbours. σωφρονισμός is the act of making someone σώφρων, sound of mind, whether by teaching or by fright.
